item.title: Canada PR wait falls for parents, rises for Express Entry applicants
item.description: Canada's latest immigration data shows shorter permanent residence waiting times for parents' sponsorship applicants, while Express Entry applicants face a two-month increase ...
item.dc:creator: Surbhi Gloria Singh
item.content:encoded: Canada has reduced waiting times for permanent residence (PR) applications in several categories, including provincial nominee and parents’ sponsorship programmes, according to the latest data released by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) on November 17. However, not all applicants have seen shorter waits. Processing times for skilled workers applying through the Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) have increased by two months, while those sponsoring their spouses are also facing longer waits. The Canadian Experience Class (CEC) processing time remained unchanged at six months, while applicants under the base Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) saw waiting times fall by one month to 12 months. The Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP) recorded a reduction of two months for applicants outside Quebec and three months for those intending to settle in the province. For applicants already in Canada who are waiting for a decision on their PR applications, a Bridging Open Work Permit (BOWP) may allow them to continue working. Those who apply before their existing work permit expires may benefit from maintained status, allowing them to work under the same conditions while their application is being processed. Canada PR processing times: Economic immigration Waiting times across most economic immigration programmes either fell or remained unchanged. The Federal Skilled Worker Program was the main exception, with processing times increasing by two months. Express Entry Processing times for the FSWP increased from seven months to nine months. The number of pending applications also rose by 1,800 to 60,100. The Canadian Experience Class (CEC), meanwhile, continued to have a six-month processing time, even as its pending applications fell by 5,700 to 48,200. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Canadian Experience Class (CEC): 6 months; unchanged.Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP): 9 months; up from 7 months.Federal Skilled Trades Program (FSTP): Not available in both updates. Service standard: Six months for all Express Entry programmes. Applications awaiting assessment: CEC: 48,200, down 5,700.FSWP: 60,100, up 1,800. Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) Applicants under the base PNP category saw processing times fall by one month to 12 months. The number of pending applications also declined by 6,300 to 90,200. For applicants applying through the Express Entry-linked enhanced PNP stream, the waiting period remained unchanged at seven months. Its pending applications increased by 700 to 13,800. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Enhanced PNP (through Express Entry): 7 months; unchanged.Base PNP (through non-Express Entry): 12 months; down from 13 months. Service standards: Six months for enhanced PNP applications and 11 months for base PNP applications. Applications awaiting assessment: Enhanced PNP: 13,800, up 700.Base PNP: 90,200, down 6,300. Under a temporary federal measure introduced on June 9, 2026, eligible PNP applicants can apply for a BOWP without waiting to receive an Acknowledgement of Receipt (AOR) for their PR application. Quebec immigration Processing times for the Quebec Business Class (QBC) fell by two months to 73 months. The Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ), however, remained unchanged at 11 months. The number of pending PSTQ applications declined by 400 to 20,100, while the QBC inventory remained unchanged at 3,600. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ): 11 months; unchanged.Quebec Business Class (QBC): 73 months; down from 75 months. Service standards: Six months for PSTQ applicants. No service standard is published for QBC applications. Applications awaiting assessment: PSTQ: 20,100, down 400.QBC: 3,600, unchanged. Atlantic Immigration Program Processing times under the Atlantic Immigration Program (AIP) fell by one month to 25 months. The number of applications awaiting assessment also declined by 400 to 11,100. Processing time (November 17; previous update: October 9): Atlantic Immigration Program: 25 months, down from 26 months. Service standard: 11 months. Applications awaiting assessment: 11,100, down 400. Other economic immigration programmes Applicants under the Start-Up Visa (SUV) and Federal Self-Employed Persons Program (FSEPP) continued to face estimated waiting times of more than 10 years. The SUV inventory fell marginally by 100 applications to 47,400, while the FSEPP backlog remained unchanged at 8,000. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Start-Up Visa (SUV): More than 10 years; unchanged.Federal Self-Employed Persons Program (FSEPP): More than 10 years; unchanged. Service standards: Not available for these programmes. Applications awaiting assessment: SUV: 47,400, down 100.FSEPP: 8,000, unchanged. Canada PR processing times: Family sponsorship Family sponsorship applicants saw mixed changes in the latest update. Waiting times for spouses and common-law partners increased by one month across all categories, while the Parents and Grandparents Program recorded shorter waiting periods. Sponsorship outside Quebec Processing times for sponsoring a spouse or common-law partner increased by one month, whether the partner was living in Canada or abroad. In contrast, the waiting period under the PGP fell by two months to 26 months. The number of applications awaiting assessment under this programme also declined by 1,800 to 33,800. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Spouse or common-law partner living in Canada: 27 months, up from 26 months.Spouse or common-law partner living outside Canada: 19 months, up from 18 months.Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP): 26 months, down from 28 months. Service standard: 12 months for sponsoring a spouse or common-law partner outside Quebec. No service standards are published for the other categories. Applications awaiting assessment: Partner living in Canada: 55,100, down 500.Partner living outside Canada: 65,900, up 300.Parents and Grandparents: 33,800, down 1,800. Sponsorship within Quebec Applicants sponsoring spouses or common-law partners who intend to settle in Quebec also faced a one-month increase in processing times. The PGP recorded a three-month reduction, with the estimated waiting period falling to 60 months. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Spouse or common-law partner living in Canada: 33 months, up from 32 months.Spouse or common-law partner living outside Canada: 34 months, up from 33 months.Parents and Grandparents Program: 60 months, down from 63 months. Service standards: IRCC does not publish service standards for family sponsorship applications involving applicants intending to settle in Quebec. Applications awaiting assessment: Partner living in Canada: 14,700, up 200.Partner living outside Canada: 19,700, up 300.Parents and Grandparents: 10,100, down 200. Canada citizenship processing times Processing times for most citizenship-related applications remained unchanged in the November update. The waiting period for a citizenship grant remained at 12 months, in line with IRCC's service standard. Applications for renunciation of citizenship continued to take four months. The processing time for searches of citizenship records improved by one month to 18 months. Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9): Citizenship grant: 12 months; unchanged.Renunciation of citizenship: 4 months; unchanged.Search of citizenship records: 18 months, down from 19 months. Service standard: 12 months for citizenship grants. IRCC reported 322,900 citizenship grant applications in its November update, an increase of 200 from October 9.

item.title: Anthropic shares tumble after record IPO as AI trade faces reality check
item.description: Anthropic shares fell nearly 9 per cent after their record $93.5 billion IPO, as concerns over stretched AI valuations and heavy spending weighed on technology stocks ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Anthropic shares tumble after record IPO as AI trade faces reality check

Anthropic shares tumble after record IPO as AI trade faces reality check Anthropic shares fell nearly 9 per cent after their record $93.5 billion IPO, as concerns over stretched AI valuations and heavy spending weighed on technology stocks

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 20 2026 | 9:06 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Anthropic's much-hyped arrival on Wall Street fizzled out on Friday, as a dramatic unravelling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector.   Widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, Anthropic's listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing after a turbulent stretch.   But the stock was last trading at $88.24, about 9 per cent below Thursday's close, while losses across other technology heavyweights suggested the IPO had done little to reverse the broader selloff.   "Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," said David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds.

Among the Magnificent Seven stocks, Nvidia and Meta Platforms fell more than 3 per cent each, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped 2 per cent and 1 per cent, respectively. Also Read

Threats, insults, settlements: How Jensen Huang made humiliation routine

Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao briefly turns billionaire after blockbuster IPO

Unsiloed AI secures $7.5 million in seed funding to scale document models

Stock Market Close: Sensex rises for 2nd day, gains 898 pts; Nifty at 25,801; bank shares lead rally

AI is giving hackers a head start. What's at risk for essential services?

Chip stocks also slid, with AMD and Sandisk down over 6 per cent each and Intel losing more than 3 per cent.   The focus now shifts to a potential OpenAI listing, which would be another major test of investors' appetite for AI stocks. OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year.   Despite a pipeline of high-profile AI and infrastructure companies, many have pushed their IPO plans to 2027.   PATIENCE MAY PAY   Anthropic's stock could find support later in the year. London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30 per cent of Anthropic's shares by year-end.

Near-term volatility, however, could persist as the initial euphoria around the listing fades and investors assess whether a valuation of about 40 times sales over the past 12 months can be sustained.   "We favour patience on Anthropic and recommend evaluating the company as it reports public results," said Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at US Bank Asset Management, adding that the current valuation "assumes years of rapid growth."   The debut has also done little to ease broader concerns about the health of the AI trade. Wall Street's main indices ended sharply lower on Thursday, while futures pointed to further declines on Friday.

PARALLELS WITH SPACEX   Anthropic's IPO has drawn parallels with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which went public in June after the second-biggest IPO on record.   Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares, surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion haul to become the biggest listing on record.   While the companies have different business models, some investors have pointed to SpaceX's sharp swings in the weeks after its debut as a reason for caution over buying Anthropic immediately after its listing.   "There's going to be some volatility like we had with SpaceX. A lot of people are going to have FOMO. I don't think there's any need to get on it on the first trade," said Rob Hackel, CEO of financial advisory and brokerage firm RF Lafferty & Co.

SpaceX shares fell more than 6 per cent.   Retail investors traded about $772 million of Anthropic shares on Thursday, the most for an IPO debut since Vanda Research began tracking the data in 2012.   The stock's sharp swings have left investors weighing whether to bet on a rebound or brace for further losses. Options trading, due to begin next week, could add to the volatility.   "It's not a good environment for Anthropic at the moment," said Carsten Hesse, head of index events at Berenberg.

TrueRE Oriana Power to invest ₹750 crore in five compressed biogas projects The renewable energy firm plans to establish five CBG plants with a combined capacity of 110 tonnes per day across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat over the next two years.

TrueRE Oriana Power plans to invest ₹750 crore in five compressed biogas projects | Image: Bloomberg

Sudheer Pal Singh New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 20 2026 | 6:55 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Renewable energy platform TrueRE Oriana Power announced that it will set up five compressed biogas (CBG) projects with a combined production capacity of 110 tonnes per day (TPD) at an investment of ₹750 crore.   The company has already registered and obtained approvals under the GOBARdhan scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, and the five plants will be set up in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat within the next two years.   These plants will strengthen the company’s presence in the green fuels segment as part of its strategy to build a diversified clean energy portfolio spanning generation, storage and consumption, it said.

"We view alternative fuels like green hydrogen, ammonia, and CBG as high potential emerging opportunities. In the next few years, we will continue to invest strategically to further increase our total production capacity,” said Rupal Gupta, managing director and chief executive officer, TrueRE Oriana Power.   The company has already delivered two projects with a capacity of 21 TPD each in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra. Beyond CBG, it is also advancing its presence in green hydrogen and its derivatives. Also Read

Scaling up CBG may save India $20 bn a year in LNG imports by 2030: Report

It has secured a 10,000-tonne-per-annum green hydrogen production award under the Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) programme and a separate award for the production and supply of 60,000 metric tonnes per annum of green ammonia. The green ammonia project has progressed through land identification and preliminary front-end engineering and design activities.

The company recently won the largest allocation in Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company's 2,000-megawatt/4,000-megawatt-hour (MWh) battery storage tender. With this win, the company’s total battery energy storage system (BESS) portfolio stands at 2.5 gigawatt-hours (GWh), with an additional pipeline of 4 GWh.   By 2030, the company is targeting 6 gigawatts (GW) of solar engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) capacity, 2.5 GW of solar independent power producer (IPP) capacity, 20 GWh of BESS capacity and 1 million tonnes per annum of e-fuels capacity.   More From This Section

item.description: Annmarie Hordern was denied access to Thursday's trilateral meeting in Shenzhen after asking Trump whether former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the US ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / China bars Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Xi meet after question on Nvidia

China bars Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Xi meet after question on Nvidia Annmarie Hordern was denied access to Thursday's trilateral meeting in Shenzhen after asking Trump whether former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the US

Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on November 19, 2026 in Shenzhen, China | Win McNamee/Pool via REUTERS

AP New York 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 20 2026 | 8:26 AM IST

Listen to This Article

It's a scenario seen every day: A reporter shouts a question out to a leader at an event. The leader either answers or ignores it. In China, though, Bloomberg TV journalist Annmarie Hordern was blocked from a key event by Chinese officials, apparently as retribution for having shouted a question in a way that the government considered rude. Hordern was barred from Thursday's trilateral meeting among President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, after having called out a question during a Trump meeting with Xi. She had asked Trump if former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the United States.

A White House official said the Chinese insisted the reporter not be allowed in despite the White House having pushed for admission. The official insisted on speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity around the issue. The White House did not immediately respond to a query about what steps it took to advocate for the reporter. Jacqui Heinrich, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, said on X that it was "commendable that the WH is advocating for press access". A pool report from the incident said the Chinese "have passed along a message that yelling questions is considered extremely rude and we will be pulled from the room if we do so".

Also Read

Musk distances from MAGA after Republican losses; Trump calls him a friend

Trump's cyber chief Sean Cairncross to step down amid repeated tech outages

Time-limited, auctioned export quotas beat blanket trade restrictions

House Democrats move to probe Trump family, top administration officials

India must turn China trade dependence into domestic value addition premium

China's Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press, and an email to Bloomberg seeking comment was not immediately returned. The incident, which reflected the way China typically seeks to tightly control news events, recalled a previous one in 2022, in which a White House pool reporter said she was knocked off balance after being yanked by her backpack when she tried to shout a question to President Joe Biden. The question was about human rights ahead of a meeting between Biden and Xi in Bali, Indonesia. The reporter lost balance without falling and was pushed towards the door, a pool report said at the time. Two White House staff members intervened and said the producer should be left alone.

China's approach to journalists, particularly foreign media, has long been chilly and uneven. In recent decades, international reporters have been expelled both for their coverage and for perceived misbehavior during news events. Resident correspondents are occasionally detained and questioned -- and in some cases in past years, compelled to sign "self-criticism" reports -- for showing up where the government doesn't want them to be. Chinese journalists who stray from the party line can face even more stringent measures, including censorship, dismissal and at times even imprisonment.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
